title: Review: Chromatography; Mass spectrometry and IR of molecules; Emission spectra and energy levels; Spectrophotometry and Beer–Lambert (AP; colorimetry for A-level); Balanced equations and reacting masses
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AS03#t2 term and clue written for the game; AM07#t1 term and clue written for the game; AN01#t2 term and clue written for the game; AM12#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM07#N.6b, AM12#N.9b, AN01#N.15, AN05#N.4, AS03#N.11, AM07#N.9, AM12#N.7, AN01#N.9, AN05#N.13, AS03#N.6b, AM07#N.14, AM12#N.12a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Emission line spectrum
items.clue: Separate bright frequencies on a dark background, given out by excited atoms.

items.label: Coefficient
items.clue: A number that multiplies a whole formula and gives the ratio of amounts in moles.

items.label: Greenhouse gas
items.clue: Takes in IR given out by the Earth's surface, then sends it out in all directions.

items.label: Standard solutions
items.clue: Samples of known concentration, all made from one stock, measured to build the line.

questions.stem: When aqueous solutions of lead(II) nitrate, Pb(NO₃)₂, and potassium iodide, KI, are mixed, a yellow precipitate of lead(II) iodide, PbI₂, forms. Which of the following is the balanced net ionic equation for the reaction?

options.text: Pb²⁺(aq) + 2 I⁻(aq) → PbI₂(aq)
K⁺(aq) + NO₃⁻(aq) → KNO₃(aq)
Pb²⁺(aq) + 2 I⁻(aq) → PbI₂(s)
Pb(aq) + I₂(aq) → PbI₂(s)

questions.explanation: Only the ions that form the precipitate. 1 Pb and 2 I each side; charge 0 each side.

questions.stem: The absorbance of a solution of a dye, measured at its wavelength of maximum absorbance in a 1.00 cm cuvette, is 0.90. A student mixes 20.0 mL of this solution with 10.0 mL of distilled water. Assuming that the volumes are additive, what is the absorbance of the diluted solution, measured in the same way?
questions.explanation: A ∝ c at fixed b and wavelength. c falls to 20.0/30.0 of its value, so A = 0.90 × 2/3 = 0.60.

questions.stem: A student proposes this model: "Any gas absorbs infrared radiation, because the particles of the gas undergo transitions to higher vibrational energy levels." The student applies the model to Ar(g) and to CO(g). Which evaluation of the model is correct?

options.text: It holds for CO only: a vibration needs a bond between atoms, which Ar atoms lack.
It holds for both: Ar atoms vibrate back and forth, just as the atoms in a CO molecule do.
It fails for both: infrared is absorbed when electrons, not atoms, move to higher levels.
It holds for Ar only: the bond in CO keeps its atoms a fixed distance apart, so they do not vibrate.

questions.stem: The dyes in a black ink are separated by paper chromatography. Which difference between the dyes is mainly responsible for the separation?

options.text: The molar mass of each dye, because lighter dye molecules are carried faster
The strength of the attractions among the molecules of each dye on its own
The relative strength of each dye's attractions to the paper and to the solvent
The size of each dye's particles, because the paper holds back the larger ones

questions.explanation: A dye moves only while dissolved in the solvent. A dye held more strongly by the paper spends more time stationary and travels a shorter distance.

questions.stem: Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere absorbs infrared radiation given off by Earth's surface, and the surrounding air becomes warmer as a result. Which reasoning best connects the absorption of infrared photons by CO₂ molecules to the warming of the air?

options.text: The photons raise CO₂ molecules to higher rotational levels, and collisions then spread this energy to other molecules.
The photons raise electrons in CO₂ to higher energy levels, and the electrons release heat as they fall back down.
The photons break the bonds in CO₂ molecules, and the energy that was stored in the bonds is released as heat.
The photons raise CO₂ molecules to higher vibrational levels, and collisions then spread this energy to other molecules.

questions.stem: A student is drawing a particulate representation of the reaction represented by the equation 2 Al(s) + 3 Cl₂(g) → 2 AlCl₃(s). The student's "before" box contains 6 Cl₂ molecules. How many Al atoms should the "before" box contain, and how many AlCl₃ formula units should the "after" box contain, if no reactant is to be left over?

options.text: 2 Al atoms and 2 AlCl₃ units
6 Al atoms and 6 AlCl₃ units
9 Al atoms and 9 AlCl₃ units
4 Al atoms and 4 AlCl₃ units

questions.explanation: 6 Cl₂ is twice the 3 Cl₂ in the equation, so twice 2 Al and twice 2 AlCl₃. Check: 12 Cl before and after.

questions.stem: A cuvette with a path length of 0.500 cm holds 3.00 mL of a 2.00 × 10⁻⁵ M solution of a dye. At the dye's wavelength of maximum absorbance, the absorbance of the solution is 0.300. What is the molar absorptivity of the dye at this wavelength?

options.text: 1.50 × 10⁴ M⁻¹ cm⁻¹
1.00 × 10⁷ M⁻¹ cm⁻¹
3.00 × 10⁴ M⁻¹ cm⁻¹
5.00 × 10³ M⁻¹ cm⁻¹

questions.explanation: ε = A ÷ (bc) = 0.300 ÷ (0.500 cm × 2.00 × 10⁻⁵ M) = 3.00 × 10⁴ M⁻¹ cm⁻¹. The 3.00 mL plays no part.

questions.stem: A student wants to compare the energies of the bond vibrations in the molecules of two different gaseous compounds. Which measurement is best aligned with this question?

options.text: Measuring the wavelengths of microwave radiation that each gas absorbs
Measuring the wavelengths of ultraviolet radiation that each gas absorbs
Measuring the wavelengths of infrared radiation that each gas absorbs
Measuring the wavelengths of visible radiation that each gas absorbs

questions.explanation: Infrared radiation is associated with transitions in vibrational levels, so the wavelengths absorbed show the energies of the bond vibrations.

questions.stem: A student runs TLC of a mixture of two polar compounds on a silica plate, using hexane as the solvent. Both spots barely leave the origin. Which change is most likely to make the spots move further up the plate and separate?

options.text: Use a longer plate and let the hexane run twice as far.
Use a solvent that is even less polar than hexane.
Spot a more concentrated sample of the mixture.
Mix some ethyl ethanoate into the hexane.

questions.explanation: Ethyl ethanoate makes the mobile phase more polar. It attracts the polar compounds more strongly, so they spend more time dissolved and less time held by the silica. They move further.

questions.stem: A green laser pointer emits light of wavelength 532 nm. What is the energy of one photon of this light?
A strip of magnesium burns brightly in air and leaves white magnesium oxide: 2Mg(s) + O₂(g) → 2MgO(s). What mass of MgO forms from 2.43 g of Mg? (Molar masses: Mg 24.31 g/mol, MgO 40.30 g/mol)

A green solution of nickel(II) ions is taken from a lab waste container. Its absorbance is measured under the same conditions as these nickel(II) standards. Standards (M : A): 0.050 : 0.16 · 0.100 : 0.32 · 0.150 : 0.48 · 0.200 : 0.64. The sample gives A = 0.40. What is its nickel(II) concentration, in M?
questions.explanation: The points lie on a straight line through the origin: A = 3.2 × c. So c = 0.40 ÷ 3.2 = 0.125. Reading across from A = 0.40 to the line gives the same value.
